message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for terminating **Visual Studio Code** (`code.exe`) from a Windows command prompt (or PowerShell) using `taskkill`.  
Feel free to copy‑paste the commands directly into your terminal.

---

## 1.  Find the process (optional)

If you want to see which instances of VS Code are running and their PIDs:

```cmd
tasklist | findstr /i code.exe
```

Typical output:

```
code.exe                 1234 Console                    1     45,678 K
code.exe                 5678 Console                    1     12,345 K
```

---

## 2.  Kill all VS Code instances

### a.  Force‑kill by image name

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

- `/IM` – match by image name (`code.exe`).  
- `/F` – force termination (no graceful shutdown).

> **Caution:** Any unsaved work in VS Code will be lost.

### b.  Force‑kill by PID (if you only want a specific one)

```cmd
taskkill /PID 1234 /F
```

Replace `1234` with the PID you obtained from `tasklist`.

---

## 3.  Kill VS Code **and** its child processes

VS Code spawns helper processes (e.g., `code.exe` for extensions).  
To terminate the whole tree:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

- `/T` – also terminate child processes.

---

## 4.  Filter by user or window title (advanced)

If you have multiple users or want to target a specific window title:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq <your_user>"
```

or

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "WINDOWTITLE eq *Visual Studio Code*"
```

---

## 5.  Using PowerShell (alternative)

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or by PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id 1234 -Force
```

---

## 6.  Quick one‑liner (if you’re scripting)

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T && echo VS Code terminated
```

---

### TL;DR

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Kill all VS Code windows immediately |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | Kill VS Code **and** all helper processes |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Kill a specific instance |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent |

Use the command that best fits your scenario. Happy coding (or closing)!
